findings.title: Capacity release proof covers only the non-terminal issuance arm
findings.evidence: `proveD110c0c1bPreDurableCapacityRelease` (tests/fixtures/phase-6b-d110c-0c1b/committed-issuance-recovery-contract.ts:333-396) issues an ordinary `pad` operation through `plane.issueLocal`, which reaches `issueOneVertex` with `requireTerminalAuthorization === false` (packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:5889). The second `capacityRejected` call site — `commitOutsideTransaction(expectedSequence)` on the terminal arm at v3-live.ts:5662, where `terminalTransactionStarted` is still false — is not executed by any test in the focused file. Its pre-durability is established only by static reading (the throw precedes both line 5663 and `registration.issuanceStore.transactIssue`).
findings.impact: The terminal-authorization branch of the corrected classification is argued rather than executed, so a future edit that moved `terminalTransactionStarted = true` above line 5662 would flip that arm to the halt branch without failing the focused file. No current behavior is wrong: with the present ordering the terminal arm is definitely pre-durable, and a regression there would still surface `graph-rejected` rather than data loss.
findings.required_action: Disposition only. Either note in the plan that terminal-arm capacity pre-durability is carried by the static ordering invariant at v3-live.ts:5662-5663, or add one terminal-authorization capacity case in a later slice. Do not expand this confirmation.

summary: Both accepted P1 findings are closed with no new P0 or P1. The production correction is exactly one line (packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:5685, `|| capacityRejected` added to the release predicate), and `capacityRejected` has a single setter at line 5651 inside `commitOutsideTransaction`, immediately followed by a throw. Both of its call sites are provably pre-durable: the terminal arm (5662) throws before `terminalTransactionStarted = true` and before `issuanceStore.transactIssue` is entered at all, and the non-terminal arm is the `buildAndSign` callback invoked at node-issuance-store.ts:600 and browser-issuance-store.ts:559 before `#commitCandidate`, outside any open transaction, with the throw neither caught nor mapped; `createTransactionalVertexIssuerCore` (protocol-v3/src/index.ts:3312) also does not wrap `transactIssue` errors, so a capacity throw can never carry code `ISSUANCE_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` and the `capacityRejected` disjunct can never pre-empt the outcome-unknown halt. Every post-commit halt is byte-identical: `committedFailure()` (5703-5711) still halts unconditionally on all nine committed arms, the outcome-unknown halt (5687) and the reservation-commit-failure halt (5813) are unchanged, and `operationAdmissionHalted` still refuses `creatorCloseRegistration` (6985) and `stageClosedBlueprintEpoch` (6655) with recovery at 7296 as the only clearing site. The tests-only capacity proof is genuine: `graph-rejected` together with observed release and no commit is jointly reachable only through the corrected catch arm, because 5686 is the sole `releaseOperationReservation` call site, `issueLocal` calls `issueOneVertex` exactly once for the single `pad` operation, and every other `graph-rejected` return either precedes `reserveOperation` (5604, 5884) or runs through `committedFailure` (5762, 5793, 5797, 5800), which never releases and would halt the close; the close is the real `bindCreatorLiveClose(...).close()` advancing to successor epoch 1. No production state is manufactured, `PARAMETERS` (maxEpochVertices 8192, maxEpochBytes 8_388_608) is untouched, the `pad` blueprint seam is a default-false tests-only flag whose consumers all pass in the retained run, and `V3OperationAdmissionPolicy` is a pre-existing export. The expanded retained roster closes the freeze omission: retained.json selects 14 paths including all five previously omitted owners plus the original nine, at 174/174 passed, 0 failed, 0 pending, success true, and the focused file passes 3/3 including the preserved committed-failure and outcome-unknown refusals. Scope is preserved across six tracked files — the one-line product change, four tests-only files, and the plan narrative — with no wire/schema, dependency, public API, authority, threshold, supported parameter, workload, campaign, or D.110a change.
